beats.title: The way back
beats.speech: Here is a mystery. A machine turns three into eleven. Can you find the way back?

beats.title: The way back
beats.speech: Hold that thought — because today it becomes mathematics. Welcome to Math Concepts Made Easy.

beats.title: The way back
beats.speech: Today is Day forty-three, and our lesson is all about inverse functions.

beats.title: The way back
beats.speech: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to find an inverse, verify it, and explain when one exists.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: Start with three. Our function first multiplies by two.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: Three times two is six.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: Then add five. Six plus five is eleven. Together, these operations define f of x equals two x plus five.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: Now start at eleven and travel backwards. Undo the last operation first: subtract five.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: Eleven minus five is six. Then undo multiplication by two: divide by two.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: Six divided by two is three. We have recovered the original input.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: The order matters. To undo multiply, then add, we must subtract, then divide.

beats.title: Undo the journey
beats.speech: This reverse journey is the inverse function. It exchanges the roles of input and output.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: Let us turn that picture into algebra. Write y equals two x plus five.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: The inverse swaps input and output. Exchange x and y: x equals two y plus five.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: Subtract five from both sides. Keep the equation balanced.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: On the right, plus five and minus five cancel. We have x minus five equals two y.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: Divide both sides by two.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: The twos cancel on the right. So y equals the quantity x minus five, divided by two.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: Name the reverse rule: f inverse of x equals the quantity x minus five, divided by two.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: Check our original number. Put eleven into the inverse: eleven minus five, all divided by two.

beats.title: Build the inverse
beats.speech: Eleven minus five is six. Six divided by two is three. The algebra matches the journey.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: A single successful number is encouraging. Composition checks every real input at once.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: First apply the inverse, then f. Replace the input of f with the entire inverse expression.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: Two times the quantity x minus five divided by two, plus five. The outside two cancels the denominator.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: That leaves x minus five plus five. The fives cancel, leaving x.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: Now check the other direction. Apply f first, then the inverse.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: Substitute two x plus five into the inverse. Subtract five from that whole expression, then divide by two.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: The fives cancel. Two x divided by two is x.

beats.title: Prove it returns x
beats.speech: Both compositions return the input. Here both functions have domain and range equal to all real numbers.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: The same swap has a geometric meaning. Here is the graph of f of x equals two x plus five.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: The point three, eleven lies on this graph: input three, output eleven.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: Swap those coordinates. Eleven, three lies on the inverse graph.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: Draw the line y equals x. Points on this line have equal coordinates.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: Reflect the function across this line. Every point a, b moves to b, a.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: The reflected graph is y equals the quantity x minus five, divided by two. The axes use exactly the same scale.

beats.title: A reflection of the same idea
beats.speech: An inverse exchanges domain and range: the possible inputs become the possible outputs.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: Does every function have an inverse function? Consider f of x equals x squared.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: Two squared is four. But negative two squared is also four.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: Reverse the arrows. Four now points to two different answers. That is not a function.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: On the graph, a horizontal line at y equals four crosses the parabola twice.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: A function is one-to-one when different inputs give different outputs. Its graph passes the horizontal line test.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: We can repair this example by restricting the original domain to x greater than or equal to zero.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: Now the reverse rule is the principal square root. Four returns only two. Its domain and range are both nonnegative.

beats.title: When the way back is ambiguous
beats.speech: The original domain restriction is essential. The square root of x squared is the absolute value of x, and equals x only when x is nonnegative.

beats.title: Inverse is not reciprocal
beats.speech: One notation trap remains. The minus one in f inverse names a reverse function. It does not mean one divided by f of x.

beats.title: Inverse is not reciprocal
beats.speech: At eleven, our inverse returns three.

beats.title: Inverse is not reciprocal
beats.speech: The reciprocal gives one divided by f of eleven. Since two times eleven plus five is twenty-seven, this is one over twenty-seven.

beats.title: Inverse is not reciprocal
beats.speech: Three and one over twenty-seven are different. Inverse means undo the mapping. Reciprocal means divide one by the output.

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: Try this one. Let g of x equal three x minus four. Find its inverse, then check it at eight.

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: Pause the video here. Which operation must you undo first?

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: Start with y equals three x minus four. Swap x and y.

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: Add four to both sides. Then divide both sides by three.

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: So g inverse of x equals the quantity x plus four, divided by three.

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: At eight, this gives eight plus four, divided by three. Twelve divided by three is four.

beats.title: Your turn
beats.speech: Check forwards: g of four equals three times four minus four. Twelve minus four is eight.

beats.title: The idea to keep
beats.speech: An inverse is the way back. Reverse the operations, in reverse order.

beats.title: The idea to keep
beats.speech: Algebraically, swap x and y, solve for y, then verify both compositions on the appropriate domains.

beats.title: The idea to keep
beats.speech: Geometrically, exchange coordinates and reflect across y equals x.

beats.title: The idea to keep
beats.speech: And always ask whether the original function is one-to-one. If necessary, restrict its domain first.

beats.title: The idea to keep
beats.speech: Three went to eleven. Eleven came back to three. That is what it means to undo a function.
